#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -g 1 -t 24h --job-name=somd-array-gpu --output=somd-array-gpu-{{id}}.{{taskid}}.out script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from -n 1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from -n 1)
# -g 1         : 1 GPU (from --gres=gpu:1)
# -t 24h       : 24 hour walltime (from --time 24:00:00)
# --job-name=somd-array-gpu : job name (derived from output filename pattern)
# --output=somd-array-gpu-{{id}}.{{taskid}}.out : output file with job ID and task ID
#
# Note: Flux uses {{id}} for job ID and {{taskid}} for array task ID
# Slurm uses %A for job array master ID and %a for task ID

# Original Slurm output: -o somd-array-gpu-%A.%a.out
# This suggests the job was intended as an array job
# Slurm: %A = job array master ID, %a = array task ID
# Flux: {{id}} = job ID, {{taskid}} = array task ID
#
# For job arrays in Flux, submit with --array option:
# flux batch --array=<range> -N 1 -n 1 -g 1 -t 24h \
#   --job-name=somd-array-gpu \
#   --output=somd-array-gpu-{{id}}.{{taskid}}.out \
#   script.sh
# Example: --array=0-9 for 10 array tasks

# Partition: main
# Slurm: -p main
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Partition selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux configuration
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Tasks: 1
# Slurm: -n 1
# Flux: -n 1 specifies 1 task

# GPU allocation: 1 GPU
# Slurm: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux: -g 1 allocates 1 GPU
# Note: GPU type cannot be specified in standard Flux syntax
# Performance impact: Job may be allocated any available GPU type

# Walltime: 24 hours
# Slurm: --time 24:00:00
# Flux: -t 24h or -t 1440m or -t 86400s

echo "CUDA DEVICES:" $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES

mkdir 10cycles
cd 10cycles

export OPENMM_PLUGIN_DIR=/home/julien/sire.app/lib/plugins/

# Execute application
# Slurm: srun launches task in allocation
# Flux: Use flux run to launch task within the batch allocation
# For single-task jobs, direct execution is also acceptable
# Using flux run for consistency with Flux task launching
flux run -n 1 -g 1 ~/sire.app/bin/somd-freenrg -C ../sim10.cfg -l 0.50 -p CUDA

cd ..

# Note on execution:
# - flux run is used instead of srun
# - -n 1 specifies 1 task (matching allocation)
# - -g 1 ensures 1 GPU is allocated to the task
# - For single-task jobs, the flux run options are technically redundant
#   with the batch allocation, but make intent explicit

# Complete submission command for regular job:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -g 1 -t 24h \
#   --job-name=somd-array-gpu \
#   --output=somd-array-gpu-{{id}}.out \
#   script.sh
#
# Complete submission command for array job (if multiple array tasks needed):
# flux batch --array=0-9 -N 1 -n 1 -g 1 -t 24h \
#   --job-name=somd-array-gpu \
#   --output=somd-array-gpu-{{id}}.{{taskid}}.out \
#   script.sh

issues: The script correctly documents resource specifications and properly converts Slurm directives to Flux command-line options.

The output file pattern uses '{{taskid}}' which is only valid for array jobs. For a single job submission (non-array), this will likely result in a literal '{{taskid}}' in the filename or an error. The documented single-job submission command should use '--output=somd-array-gpu-{{id}}.out' without the taskid component.

The 'flux run' command inside the batch script specifies '-n 1 -g 1' which is redundant when the batch allocation already provides these resources. While not incorrect, this could be simplified to just 'flux run ~/sire.app/bin/somd-freenrg ...' to use all allocated resources.
The script creates a directory '10cycles' without checking if it already exists. Consider using 'mkdir -p 10cycles' to avoid errors on repeated runs.
No memory specification is included. For GPU-accelerated molecular dynamics with OpenMM, explicit memory allocation may be beneficial to ensure sufficient resources.
The script does not validate that CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is properly set by Flux before proceeding. Consider adding a check or validation step.

The script changes directory multiple times (cd 10cycles, then cd ..). The final 'cd ..' assumes the script started in a specific location. If the batch submission uses --cwd or the script is called from a different location, this could cause unexpected behavior.

For array jobs, the script does not use any array-specific logic (like referencing FLUX_TASK_ID or similar). If this is intended to be an array job, the script should likely use the array task ID to differentiate between runs.
The 24-hour walltime is quite long. Verify this is within the site's maximum walltime limits.

echo "CUDA DEVICES:" $CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES

mkdir 10cycles

export OPENMM_PLUGIN_DIR=/home/julien/sire.app/lib/plugins/
